Chapter 7: System Testing

7.1 Testing Strategy, Methodology & Test Environment

Quality assurance for AssetDesk was executed through a comprehensive, multi-tiered testing strategy structured around the automated test pyramid. Verification combined white-box unit testing for business rules and state machines, black-box HTTP integration testing for REST API controllers, end-to-end browser automation for full user journeys, and defensive security assertion testing. Testing tools comprised Jest 29.7.0, Supertest 7.0.0, mongodb-memory-server 10.1.3, and Microsoft Playwright 1.50.0.

Table 7.1: Automated Test Environment Specifications
Environment Dimension Specification / Version Role in Verification Lifecycle
Operating System Darwin 24.6.0 (x64) POSIX-compliant continuous testing baseline environment
JavaScript Runtime Node.js v24.13.0 / npm 11.6.2 Execution engine for backend unit and integration test runners
Database Layer MongoDB Community Server v8.2.4 Isolated in-memory database instance (mongodb-memory-server)
Browser Engine Chromium 131.0 (Headless) Headless browser running 16 Playwright E2E tests at 1366×768
Test Runners Jest 29.7.0 & Playwright 1.50.0 Parallel test runners with Istanbul code coverage instrumentation
Quality Assurance Acceptance Criteria

The test strategy enforced four mandatory pass criteria prior to build approval: (1) 100% pass rate across all 272 automated test assertions with zero skipped or flaky tests; (2) Line and statement code coverage exceeding the 85% project contract threshold; (3) Complete traceability connecting all 20 Functional Requirements (FR-01..FR-20) to automated tests; (4) Average API query response latencies remaining strictly under 10ms for inventory pagination and summary endpoints.

7.5 Defect Resolution, Code Improvement & Performance Benchmarks

Defect logging and resolution were tracked systematically throughout the test-driven implementation. Table 7.7 records primary engineering defects resolved, while Table 7.8 presents empirical benchmark latency metrics captured across 50 continuous samples per endpoint.

Table 7.7: Defect Tracking & Engineering Resolution History (from BUILD_LOG.md)
Defect Encountered Root Cause Diagnosis Engineering Resolution Applied Re-Test Result
Seed Reset Audit Lock Block AuditLog.deleteMany({}) was blocked by append-only immutability pre-hook during re-seed. Introduced bypassAuditLock: true query option for admin maintenance scripts in AuditLog.js. Verified (UT-29)
License Masking Suffix Mismatch Fixture key KEY-EXP-001 had 3-digit suffix resulting in malformed mask ****-****--001. Standardized fixture to 4-digit suffix KEY-EXP-0001 matching contract specifications. Verified (SEC-09)
Closed Ticket Precedence Error Employee status mutation on closed ticket returned HTTP 403 instead of required 400 Bad Request. Prioritized closed ticket immutability guard before role-specific status transition checks. Verified (UT-40)
E2E Rate Limiter Flakiness Automated Playwright tests triggered express-rate-limit 429 block on login during test suites. Added secure internal test header bypass (x-playwright-test) during automated runs. Verified (ST-01..16)
Table 7.8: API Endpoint Latency Benchmark (50 Continuous Samples, performance.json)
Target REST API Endpoint Min Latency Avg Latency P95 Latency Max Latency SOP Target
POST /auth/login 70.13 ms 75.82 ms 81.36 ms 183.67 ms < 100 ms (Pass)
GET /assets?limit=10 4.89 ms 7.49 ms 9.07 ms 17.50 ms < 10 ms (Pass)
GET /tickets?limit=10 5.65 ms 7.96 ms 10.33 ms 11.10 ms < 10 ms (Pass)

Benchmark Hardware Environment & Methodology: Benchmarks were measured using server/scripts/measure.js on an Intel Core i5-10400 CPU @ 2.90GHz (12 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM) running Node.js v24.13.0 on Darwin 24.6.0. The 75.82ms login latency reflects CPU-bound bcrypt salt computations (10 rounds), while all inventory and query endpoints maintained average latencies under 10ms. These development metrics provide a high-fidelity baseline; multi-tenant production hosting behind reverse proxies may introduce minor network transport variance.
Quality Assurance Sign-Off: With 272 automated test assertions passing, 87.16% statement coverage, zero open critical defects, and sub-10ms operational response times, the AssetDesk system fully satisfies all technical verification criteria defined in the project contract and VICAIT SOP Section 2.2.
